Giulia

The model seems properly specify. We can follow by evaluating overall and local model fit.

Overall: this function will present the posterior distribution of the absolute approximate fit indices. If you want the relative ones you will need to estimate a null model, see ?blavFitIndices
From simulations, the most recommended approximate fit indices are gamma-hat and CFI
Garnier-Villarreal, M., & Jorgensen, T. D. (2020). Adapting Fit Indices for Bayesian Structural Equation Modeling: Comparison to Maximum Likelihood. Psychological Methods, 25(1), 46–70. https://doi.org/dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000224

## The default method mimics fit indices derived from ML estimation
ML <- blavFitIndices(fitBSEM2)
ML
summary(ML, prob=.95,central.tendency = c("mean","median"))

you can get the Bayesian Information criteria from
fitMeasures(fitBSEM2)
these are hardly interpretable by themselves, but are the best ones for model comparison with the blavCompare() function

For local model fit you can get posterior distributions from modification indices this way
##############
##### modification indices
##############
discFUN_mi <- list(
  mod.ind_mi = function(object){
    temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
    mods <- temp$mi
    names(mods) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs,temp$group)
    return(mods)
  },mod.ind_epc = function(object){
    temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
    epc <- temp$epc
    names(epc) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs,temp$group)
    return(epc )
  },mod.ind_sepc.all = function(object){
    temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
    sepc.all <- temp$sepc.all
    names(sepc.all) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs,temp$group)
    return(sepc.all )
  }
)



## PPMC for each
out_mi <- ppmc(fitBSEM2, thin = 5, discFUN = discFUN_mi)

summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_mi",
        sort.by = "EAP", decreasing=T)
summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_mi",
        sort.by = "Median", decreasing=T)

summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_epc",
        sort.by = "EAP", decreasing=T)
summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_sepc.all",
        sort.by = "EAP", decreasing=T)

Il giorno sabato 4 luglio 2020 18:31:43 UTC+2, Mauricio Garnier-Villarreal ha scritto:
Giulia

The model seems properly specify. We can follow by evaluating overall and local model fit.

Overall: this function will present the posterior distribution of the absolute approximate fit indices. If you want the relative ones you will need to estimate a null model, see ?blavFitIndices
From simulations, the most recommended approximate fit indices are gamma-hat and CFI
Garnier-Villarreal, M., & Jorgensen, T. D. (2020). Adapting Fit Indices for Bayesian Structural Equation Modeling: Comparison to Maximum Likelihood. Psychological Methods, 25(1), 46–70. https://doi.org/dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000224

## The default method mimics fit indices derived from ML estimation
ML <- blavFitIndices(fitBSEM2)
ML
summary(ML, prob=.95,central.tendency = c("mean","median"))

you can get the Bayesian Information criteria from
fitMeasures(fitBSEM2)
these are hardly interpretable by themselves, but are the best ones for model comparison with the blavCompare() function

For local model fit you can get posterior distributions from modification indices this way
##############
##### modification indices
##############
discFUN_mi <- list(
  mod.ind_mi = function(object){
    temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
    mods <- temp$mi
    names(mods) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs,temp$group)
    return(mods)
  },mod.ind_epc = function(object){
    temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
    epc <- temp$epc
    names(epc) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs,temp$group)
    return(epc )
  },mod.ind_sepc.all = function(object){
    temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
    sepc.all <- temp$sepc.all
    names(sepc.all) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs,temp$group)
    return(sepc.all )
  }
)



## PPMC for each
out_mi <- ppmc(fitBSEM2, thin = 5, discFUN = discFUN_mi)

summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_mi",
        sort.by = "EAP", decreasing=T)
summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_mi",
        sort.by = "Median", decreasing=T)

summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_epc",
        sort.by = "EAP", decreasing=T)
summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_sepc.all",
        sort.by = "EAP", decreasing=T)


Hope this is useful

Giulia

The model seems properly specify. We can follow by evaluating overall and local model fit.

Overall: this function will present the posterior distribution of the absolute approximate fit indices. If you want the relative ones you will need to estimate a null model, see ?blavFitIndices
From simulations, the most recommended approximate fit indices are gamma-hat and CFI
Garnier-Villarreal, M., & Jorgensen, T. D. (2020). Adapting Fit Indices for Bayesian Structural Equation Modeling: Comparison to Maximum Likelihood. Psychological Methods, 25(1), 46–70. https://doi.org/dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000224

## The default method mimics fit indices derived from ML estimation
ML <- blavFitIndices(fitBSEM2)
ML
summary(ML, prob=.95,central.tendency = c("mean","median"))

you can get the Bayesian Information criteria from
fitMeasures(fitBSEM2)
these are hardly interpretable by themselves, but are the best ones for model comparison with the blavCompare() function

For local model fit you can get posterior distributions from modification indices this way
##############
##### modification indices
##############
discFUN_mi <- list(
  mod.ind_mi = function(object){
    temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
    mods <- temp$mi
    names(mods) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs,temp$group)
    return(mods)
  },mod.ind_epc = function(object){
    temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
    epc <- temp$epc
    names(epc) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs,temp$group)
    return(epc )
  },mod.ind_sepc.all = function(object){
    temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
    sepc.all <- temp$sepc.all
    names(sepc.all) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs,temp$group)
    return(sepc.all )
  }
)



## PPMC for each
out_mi <- ppmc(fitBSEM2, thin = 5, discFUN = discFUN_mi)

summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_mi",
        sort.by = "EAP", decreasing=T)
summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_mi",
        sort.by = "Median", decreasing=T)

summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_epc",
        sort.by = "EAP", decreasing=T)
summary(out_mi, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_sepc.all",
        sort.by = "EAP", decreasing=T)


Hope this is useful

The model seems properly specify. We can follow by evaluating overall and local model fit.

Overall: this function will present the posterior distribution of the absolute approximate fit indices. If you want the relative ones you will need to estimate a null model, see ?blavFitIndices
From simulations, the most recommended approximate fit indices are gamma-hat and CFI
Garnier-Villarreal, M., & Jorgensen, T. D. (2020). Adapting Fit Indices for Bayesian Structural Equation Modeling: Comparison to Maximum Likelihood. Psychological Methods, 25(1), 46–70. https://doi.org/dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000224

## The default method mimics fit indices derived from ML estimation
ML <- blavFitIndices(fitBSEM2)
ML
summary(ML, prob=.95,central.tendency = c("mean","median"))

you can get the Bayesian Information criteria from
fitMeasures(fitBSEM2)
these are hardly interpretable by themselves, but are the best ones for model comparison with the blavCompare() function

Giulia

It seems the summary output its working now.

A quick note about the overall fit indices (blavFitIndices), the once that have shown to be less sensitive to other characteristics other than misfit are GammaHat and CFI, so these are the most recommended once

Now, the issue on how to interpret modification indices is more complicated, as there is no consensus about how to interpret and which parameters to include based on modification indices. Whitaker (2012) recommendation is to look at both mi and sepc, and make a decision if both provide solid information for the addition of this parameter. Also, always take into consideration if the addition of this parameter is theoretically relevant.

So, the simplest recommendation would be:
- Which paremeters show the largest mi change, and does the credible interval shows values in the high range?
- Which paremeters show high sepc, and does the credible interval shows values higher than |0.1|?

If you have parameters that passed these 2 criteria, would be suggested that the model is indicating that this parameter should be included. This comes from taking Whitaker suggestion and adding the interpretation of credible intervals.
We are in the process of doing more specific research to give more clear recommendations

Note, that sepc is an approximate of what the standardized parameter could be, so it does not neccesarily would be that when included, and in cases can show out of bounds values (higher than |1| )
Also, for the sepc, and epc, the summary is sorting them by EAP, but you have to look both the highest positive and highest negative values, so make sure to check the top and tail of the sort table


Hope this helps


Whittaker, T. A. (2012). Using the Modification Index and Standardized Expected Parameter Change for Model Modification. The Journal of Experimental Education, 80(1), 26–44. https://doi.org/10.1080/00220973.2010.531299

The model seems properly specify. We can follow by evaluating overall and local model fit.

Overall: this function will present the posterior distribution of the absolute approximate fit indices. If you want the relative ones you will need to estimate a null model, see ?blavFitIndices
From simulations, the most recommended approximate fit indices are gamma-hat and CFI
Garnier-Villarreal, M., & Jorgensen, T. D. (2020). Adapting Fit Indices for Bayesian Structural Equation Modeling: Comparison to Maximum Likelihood. Psychological Methods, 25(1), 46–70. https://doi.org/dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000224

ML <- blavFitIndices(fitBSEM2)
ML

you can get the Bayesian Information criteria from
fitMeasures(fitBSEM2)
these are hardly interpretable by themselves, but are the best ones for model comparison with the blavCompare() function
